html:
The Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya in Bihar marks the place where the Buddha is said to have reached enlightenment while sitting under a fig tree. It is the holiest site of Buddhism.

Ashoka came here about 260 BCE and built the first shrine and a polished stone seat, the Diamond Throne, which survives. The present temple is a brick tower 55 metres high with four smaller towers at its corners. It dates from the 5th or 6th century CE, in the time of the Guptas or just after, and is one of the oldest brick temples still standing in India.

The Bodhi tree beside it is counted as a descendant of the first. A cutting was taken to Sri Lanka in Ashoka's time (see Mahinda's mission), and the tree at Bodh Gaya was later replanted from that line.

Pilgrims came from across Asia; kings of Burma paid for repairs more than once. After Buddhism faded in India around 1200 the temple fell into ruin and a Hindu monastery took charge of it. British engineers restored it in the 1880s, and Anagarika Dharmapala began a long campaign to return it to Buddhists. A joint committee has run it since 1949.
sum: The Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya in Bihar marks the place where the Buddha is said to have reached enlightenment while sitting under a fig tree. It is the holiest site of Buddhism.
